argument_summary: The certification position is narrower than a clean readiness claim. The admissible record supports only a caveated certification packet: aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout includes monitoring and rollback, but the mortgage servicing assistant hardship-forbearance limitation remains exposed and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. Under that record, the defensible packet is one that certifies only with explicit disclosure of the material limitation, not one that treats rollout controls as sufficient by themselves.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the position. The narrow certification theory stands or falls on the policy and admissible evidence, not on launch-velocity considerations.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the controlling point. It says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining continued exposure. The admissible evidence shows neither condition is met here, because the affected segment remains in scope and the only risk-acceptance item is an incomplete draft that does not address that segment. The same policy also says disclosure is still required when the exposed segment remains in launch scope. So the supportable position is caveated compliance through explicit limitation disclosure, not clean compliance and not a theory that 5% rollout, rollback, or dashboards remove the disclosure duty.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the required explicit disclosure has already been completed in the final model card or certification packet.
There is no approved risk acceptance in evidence that specifically addresses the exposed mortgage servicing assistant segment.
Rollout controls, monitoring, rollback, and a small initial percentage do not by themselves satisfy the policy predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
